Mere Mola Ke Bhi Mola Tera Syed Mohammad Shah.

1
Mere Maula Mere Maula Ke Bhi Maula Tera.
Lab Pe Zahra-o-Ali Ke Bhi Hai Kalma Tera.
Jalwa Gar Dekhi Hai Tauheed-o-Imamat Iss Par.
Toor Our Arsh Se Bhi Oncha Hai Shana Tera.
Dono La Raib Hain Yeh Bhi Hai Ali Woh Bhi Ali.
Aik ALLAH Tera Aik Hai Banda Tera.

2
Dein Kabhi Ghar-e-Hira Se Nahi Aata Bahir.
Sath Deti Na Agar Madar-e-Zahra Tera.
Pusht Pe Aaye Jo Shabeer Tu Hota Hai Taveel.
Kitna Shabeer Se Manoos Hai Sajdah Tera.
Palney Walay Ko Rab Kehte Hain Jab Ahl-e-Lughaat.
Yaad Aata Hai Mujhe Palney Wala Tera.

3
Aik Sheeshi Mein Jahan Khak-e-Shifa Rakhi Gayi.
Sab Se Pehla Tu Azakhana Hai Hujra Tera.
Kis Tarha Aal Ka Nabiyon Se Taqabul Ho Bhala.
Yeh Tera Khon Hai Our Woh Hai Paseena Tera.
Faisla Ashk-e-Azza Dekh Ke Hoga Muhsin.
Kaun Hai Ghair Tera Kaun Hai Apna Tera.

from pathlib import Path
p = Path(\"src/data/lyrics/mere-mola-ke-bhi-mola-tera-syed-mohammad-shah-naat-tajpoints-4cde319cb021492ff57d.md\")
_, meta, body = p.read_text().split('---', 2)
roman = meta.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n')[1]
for lyrics, digits in [(roman, '123'), (body, '۱۲۳')]:
    opening, *stanzas = [b.splitlines() for b in lyrics.strip().split('\\n\\n')]
    assert len(opening) == 1
    assert [s[0].strip() for s in stanzas] == list(digits)
    assert [len(s) - 1 for s in stanzas] == [6, 6, 6]
assert all(not line or line.startswith('  ') for line in roman.splitlines())
assert '\\u200c' not in body
print('Opening and three six-verse stanzas verified in both scripts.')
PY"

item.text:
Reconstructed the Urdu-script title and lyrics in the selected Markdown file, set the direction to RTL, and removed the `noUrdu` tag. Preserved the Roman wording in `romanLyrics`, adjusting only capitalization and verse-final periods.

Verified that both versions have one opening line and three six-verse stanzas. I read the ambiguous Roman “shana” as **شانہ** (shoulder).
